title: Rijksmuseum
blurb: Pierre Cuypers’s 1885 national museum: red brick Gothic-Renaissance facades around two atrium courts, a public passage through the middle, twin towers, and the Gallery of Honour on the second floor.

systems.name: Facades
systems.description: Red brick facades in bays with stone bands, combining Gothic and Renaissance motifs.

systems.name: Central passage
systems.description: The public tunnel through the building’s central axis, open to cyclists and pedestrians.

systems.name: Towers
systems.description: Twin towers flanking the central passage, four corner towers, and the central roof spire.

systems.name: Roofs and gables
systems.description: Roof sections, skylights, decorative gables, dormers and chimneys.

systems.name: Atriums
systems.description: The two interior courtyards at the centre of each square.

systems.name: Interiors
systems.description: The Gallery of Honour, the Night Watch hall, the Great Hall and the library.

systems.name: Floor plates
systems.description: Floor plates marking the museum levels from the first to the third floor.

systems.name: Decoration
systems.description: Sculptures, tile pictures, and stained glass.

systems.name: Wings and garden
systems.description: Philips wing, Asian pavilion and museum garden.

floors.name: Basement
floors.description: Foundations below ground level; the public route starts on the ground floor.

floors.name: Ground floor (Floor 0)
floors.description: Entrance, atrium, passage and the 1100 to 1600 galleries.

floors.name: First floor (Floor 1)
floors.description: The 1700 to 1900 galleries and the Cuypers Library viewing gallery.

floors.name: Second floor (Floor 2)
floors.description: The 17th century, the Gallery of Honour, the Great Hall and the Night Watch Room.

floors.name: Roof and towers
floors.description: Roofs, skylights, gables and towers above the eaves.
